newsitem.title: USA: USWC prods prices fall amid thin local trade.
newsitem.headline: USWC prods prices fall amid thin local trade.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast products were mixed Tuesday, with traders sidelined most of the day waiting for inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API), traders said.
Meanwhile, the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), saw slight gains, with unleaded gasoline futures for August delivery up a 0.98 cents a gallon to 58.92 cents.
Los Angeles CARB gasoline remained 54.50/55.50 cents a gallon with San Francisco CARB two cents a gallon higher, gaining one cent from yesterday as exports continue to tighten Bay area supplies.

Exports, about 10 cargoes since late May, have resulted from weak profits at West Coast refineries, where the cost of raw material -- crude oil -- has greatly surpassed what refiners can fetch for products.
Traders said most cargoes were sized around 245,000 barrels and are being shipped to the Far East and southeast U.S markets.
Buyers of conventional grade gasoline, for sale in Reno, Nevada, offered to pay one cent less than Monday, or 51 cents a gallon, traders said.
Reformulated gasoline, for sale in the metropolitan Phoenix area, was talked one cent below CARB levels,traders said.
